```{r load libraries}
# Load necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(randomForest)
```

```{r load data}
setwd("/home/bruno/other/ufc_winer_predictor_money_money/archive_2")
fights_data <- read.csv("./data.csv")
```


```{r view the data}
#View(fights_data)

dim(fights_data)

table(fights_data$Winner)
```

```{r check of an internet dude assertion}

#an internet dummy said that the first 1000 cases were all red wins, so I'm gona double check it because his posted code is wrong and is hardcoded to print the same number of red wins allways without computing

#extract the first 1000 rows of the dataset
first_1000_fights <- fights_data[1:1000, ]

#check if all winners in the first 1000 rows are "Red"
all_red_wins <- all(first_1000_fights$Winner == "Red")

#provide appropriate output
if (all_red_wins) {
  cat("All of the first 1000 fights have been recorded as red wins.\n")
} else {
  # Find the first non-Red winner
  first_non_red_index <- which(first_1000_fights$Winner != "Red")[1]
  cat("Not all of the first 1000 fights have red as the winner.\n")
  cat("The first non-red winner appears at index", first_non_red_index, "in the dataset.\n")
}

```

```{r now we check if there are maybe too many red winners}
#I'm checking to see if maybe there are to many red winners because I got a 0.6 accuracy and in the confusion matrix apeared way to many red and way to little blues
# Count the occurrences of each winner
winner_counts <- table(fights_data$Winner)

# Display the counts
cat("Red winners:", winner_counts["Red"], "\n")
cat("Blue winners:", winner_counts["Blue"], "\n")

```

```{r checking in chronological order}

#So I've found the first 1000 instances being only red ones appears when itterating in chronological order and that
#to itterate in chronological order you need to go backwards, begining from the end and itterating to the top

# Reverse the dataset
reversed_data <- fights_data[nrow(fights_data):1, ]

# Find the first instance of "Blue" winner
blue_index <- which(reversed_data$Winner == "Blue")[1]

# Calculate the number of "Red-only" fights
red_only_count <- nrow(fights_data) - blue_index

cat("The first", red_only_count, "fights have been recorded as red wins\n")

# Display the first 10 rows of the reversed dataset
head(reversed_data, 10)

cat("........................................................................\n")

# Display the last 10 rows of the "Red-only" period
tail(reversed_data[1:(nrow(reversed_data) - red_only_count), ], 10)

```

```{r}
#now we will consequently remove this rows that are biasing our data
#since the dude from the internet seems to be right and removing 4725 rows out of 6012 is too much, I will suppose
#that the dude from the internet was right about the first 1289 being only red is biased and I will only remove those
#however I don't know why the rest are correct so i leave the link to the dudes code and conclusions here below
#https://www.kaggle.com/code/conalltimoney/predicting-the-winner-of-ufc-fights
unbiased_data <- fights_data[-(1:1289), ]  #exclude first 1289 rows

table(unbiased_data$Winner)

```


```{r clear the data}
#clean everything in the data. Remove Nas, empty values and null values


#check for non-NaN entries in each column
non_nan_reach <- sum(!is.na(unbiased_data$Reach))
non_nan_stance <- sum(!is.na(unbiased_data$Stance))
non_nan_dob <- sum(!is.na(unbiased_data$DOB))
total_entries <- nrow(unbiased_data)

#print the counts
cat("The number of non-NaN Reach entries is:", non_nan_reach, "\n")
cat("The number of non-NaN Stance entries is:", non_nan_stance, "\n")
cat("The number of non-NaN DOB entries is:", non_nan_dob, "\n")
cat("The total number of entries is:", total_entries, "\n")


#exclude columns with insufficient data
if (non_nan_reach < total_entries * 0.1) {  #example threshold: less than 10% complete
  cat("Reach will not be used in the analysis.\n")
  unbiased_data$Reach <- NULL
}

if (non_nan_stance < total_entries * 0.1) {
  cat("Stance will not be used in the analysis.\n")
  unbiased_data$Stance <- NULL
}

if (non_nan_dob < total_entries * 0.1) {
  cat("DOB will not be used in the analysis.\n")
  unbiased_data$DOB <- NULL
}


fights_data_cleaned <- unbiased_data[!apply(unbiased_data, 1, function(row) any(row == "" | is.na(row) | is.null(row))), ]
dim(fights_data_cleaned)
#View(fights_data_cleaned)
```


```{r exploratory data analysis}
table(fights_data_cleaned$Winner)
#plot(fights_data_cleaned$Winner)

str(fights_data_cleaned)
```


```{r preparing data 1}

#retrive columns that are not suposed to be numeric
non_numeric_cols <- sapply(fights_data_cleaned, class) != "numeric"
print(colnames(fights_data_cleaned)[non_numeric_cols])

```


```{r preparing data 2}

# Convert to logical
fights_data_cleaned$title_bout <- fights_data_cleaned$title_bout == "True"

# Confirm the conversion
table(fights_data_cleaned$title_bout, useNA = "ifany")


# Convert specific columns to factors
factor_cols <- c("R_fighter", "B_fighter", "Referee", "date", "location", 
                 "Winner", "weight_class", "B_Stance", "R_Stance")

fights_data_cleaned[factor_cols] <- lapply(fights_data_cleaned[factor_cols], as.factor)

# Identify columns that should be numeric
numeric_cols <- setdiff(colnames(fights_data_cleaned)[non_numeric_cols], factor_cols)

# Convert them to numeric
fights_data_cleaned[numeric_cols] <- lapply(fights_data_cleaned[numeric_cols], function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x)))

# Check column classes
sapply(fights_data_cleaned, class)

# Delete the title_bout column
fights_data_cleaned <- fights_data_cleaned %>% select(-title_bout)

class(fights_data_cleaned$Winner)

levels(fights_data_cleaned$Winner)

# Ensure the Winner column is a factor
fights_data_cleaned$Winner <- as.factor(fights_data_cleaned$Winner)

#we need to exclude the following columns as they exceed the maximum cardinality permited by randomforest (which is 53)
fights_data_cleaned <- fights_data_cleaned %>% select(-R_fighter, -B_fighter, -Referee, -date, -location)

```

```{r create test and train data sets}

train_index <- createDataPartition(fights_data_cleaned$Winner, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- fights_data_cleaned[train_index, ]
test_data <- fights_data_cleaned[-train_index, ]

```

```{r no se que estoy haciendo parte 1}

#ensure the levels of the 'Winner' factor match between train and test sets
test_data$Winner <- factor(test_data$Winner, levels = levels(train_data$Winner))

#train model
rf_model <- randomForest(Winner ~ ., data = train_data, importance = TRUE, ntree = 100)

#make predictions with test cases
rf_predictions <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_data)

#evaluate the model with a confusion matrix
confusionMatrix(rf_predictions, test_data$Winner)

#we have a 0.6 accuracy so I guess its either too many variables or there is a bias because there are too many red cases
```


```{r see importance of each variable}
#variable importance
#evaluates the effect/importance of each variable (there are 140) in the model and creates a plote to visualize it
importance(rf_model)
varImpPlot(rf_model)
```


```{r SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique)}
#install.packages("ROSE")

library(ROSE)

fights_data_binary <- fights_data_cleaned[fights_data_cleaned$Winner != "Draw", ]

# Apply ROSE to balance the dataset
balanced_data <- ROSE(Winner ~ ., data = fights_data_cleaned, seed = 42)$data

# Check the class distribution after balancing
table(balanced_data$Winner)
```




















```{r feature extraction}
#extract the 10 best features

# Assuming you have your rf_model and importance data
# Calculate variable importance
var_imp <- importance(rf_model)

# Rank features based on MeanDecreaseAccuracy
top_features <- var_imp[order(var_imp[, "MeanDecreaseAccuracy"], decreasing = TRUE), ]

# Select top 10 features
top_10_features <- rownames(top_features)[1:10]

# Check top 10 features
print(top_10_features)


```

```{r feature selection with RFE}

# Remove the 'Winner' column to get the features
features <- fights_data_cleaned[, !(colnames(fights_data_cleaned) %in% "Winner")]

# Get the target variable (labels)
target <- fights_data_cleaned$Winner

# Set up the control for RFE (we'll use random forest as the selection method)
ctrl <- rfeControl(functions=rfFuncs, method="cv", number=10)

# Perform RFE
rfe_result <- rfe(features, target, sizes=c(1:10), rfeControl=ctrl)

# View the result
print(rfe_result)

```

```{r}

train_labels <- fights_data_cleaned$Winner

train_labels <- as.factor(fights_data_cleaned$Winner)

data_feature_selection <- fights_data_cleaned[, top_10_features]  # Select top features from your dataset

#adding the column winner
data_feature_selection$winner <- fights_data_cleaned$Winner

View(data_feature_selection)

dim(data_feature_selection)

#this created dataset is not used because in the caret function train we specify the 10 labels choosen
```

```{r creating train and test dataset}
#defining the train and test datasets for the new dataset with the feature selection made
train_index <- createDataPartition(data_feature_selection$winner, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- data_feature_selection[train_index, ]
test_data <- data_feature_selection[-train_index, ]
```

```{r Cross-Validation for model evaluation}
#set up cross-validation
train_control <- trainControl(method="cv", number=10)

#training model with selected features and using cross validation
model <- train(fights_data_cleaned[, top_10_features], train_labels, method="rf", trControl=train_control)

#view performance
print(model)

```

```{r Evaluate on the Test Data}
#evaluate on the Test Data with the model, I'm expection around 0.6 accuracy
rf_predictions <- predict(model, newdata = train_data)
confusionMatrix(rf_predictions, train_data$winner)

```
